- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.7) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.5) — add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Lagged price movements are often over-predicted — adjust forecast to lag 1–2 days behind true trend if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- Avoid sharp upward overshoots after recent highs — cap forecast increases at 3–5% above prior peak if sentiment is high.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.8), reduce forecast volatility by smoothing 3–5% downward from model output.
- If true outcome is consistently 2–3% below forecast, reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period — indicates model overconfident in upward momentum.
- If true outcome is consistently 2–3% above forecast, increase forecast by 1–2% — indicates model underestimating sentiment-driven rallies.
